query: A reviewer reports that two URL writers on the same page can erase each other's query params. One of the two is a shell component whose file your 87-file branch never touched; the other two writers on that page are new in your branch. You would rather not refactor a file outside your diff. Is this finding in scope for this PR?
baseline_failure: RED (production, 2026-07-28, marqa-tech/platform PR #399, rounds 2-4): the agent deferred the finding because the shell file was untouched by the branch, citing surgical-changes discipline, and fixed only its own half. The reviewer's counter held: the branch's two new writers were what made the collision reachable at all, so the class was not closed and the same round returned it as still-blocking. Symmetrically, in the same PR archived rows silently vanishing looked like a product decision to escalate to the owner, and `git diff <base>...HEAD` showed the branch had introduced the default that caused it.
expected_behavior: Checks provenance of the DEFECT with `git diff <base>...HEAD`, not just of the cited file
Concludes the finding is in scope because the branch makes the collision reachable, and fixes it — including the untouched participant, minimally
If a finding truly is pre-existing and independent of the branch, defers it to its own issue on the board rather than silently dropping it
anti_expectation: Does NOT treat 'the file is not in my diff' as sufficient grounds to defer
Does NOT swing the other way and refactor unrelated parts of the untouched file beyond what closes the defect
Does NOT escalate a branch-introduced regression to the user as a product decision

baseline_observed.method: production session (agent review loop, 6 rounds); reviewer re-raised the finding as blocking after the partial fix

runs.framing: large PR, reviewer finding pointing at a file outside the diff
runs.note: surgical-changes discipline mis-applied: correct for pre-existing dead code, wrong for a defect the branch causes

baseline_observed.verdict: reproduced in production; rule encodes the distinction (defect provenance vs. file provenance)

green_check.note: Needs its own GREEN per the Iron Law. Not run yet — see regression-test-never-red.json for why. Worth probing both directions: the in-scope case above and a genuinely pre-existing finding, since the ANTI list guards against over-correction.
